propositions: Cloud probe hardcodes RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES instead of reading from runtime config, unlike DC reconciler which sources resolved_statuses from configuration.

A Cloud tenant with non-standard resolved-status names (e.g. 'Closed', 'Complete', "Won't Do") cannot customize the set without code changes, causing misclassification of issues as PRESENT_FILTERED instead of PRESENT_RESOLVED.

JiraConfig must expose resolved_statuses as a configurable list[str] field with default values ["Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"], parsed via _as_str_list coercer from [tool.rebar.jira] and REBAR_JIRA_RESOLVED_STATUSES env override.

The probe classify_probe_response function must resolve the status set from config at runtime, falling back to module-level RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES when the configured list is empty, unset, or encounters ConfigError.
An explicitly empty jira.resolved_statuses config must fall back to the module default rather than binding an empty frozenset, mirroring DC's settings.py guard logic.
